category_title: Students with aggressive behaviors and impulse control difficulties in urban environments
minimal_context: Dominic is playing at the sensory table with small plastic animals and other children during free choice time.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is free choice time, so you can play at the sensory table with the small plastic animals and your classmates.

STUDENT: (Picks up the plastic animals from the sensory table) This is a bear, roar! And this is a wolf, awooo!

TUTOR: Keep playing with the animals.

STUDENT: (Continues playing for a long period of time, then suddenly moves his animals into another child's space) The bear is coming over here now.

TUTOR: Remember to share the space at the table.

STUDENT: (Hits the child next to him) No, I need those! (Takes the other plastic animals away from the child)

options.A: Play with the small plastic animals in the sensory table during the free choice activity.
options.B: Use follow-in comments to describe the tutor's own actions or the student's actions at the sensory table.
options.C: Deliver brief (3-5 s) statements of attention contingent on the hitting (e.g., "You will hurt your friend, don't do that.").
options.D: Provide visual expectations or rules and a visual chart with the time on it for the sensory table.
